title.justification: This is the given title of the paper, which presents a benchmark for evaluating the capabilities of Graph Neural Networks and Transformers in capturing long-range dependencies.

extractions.description: The paper presents the Long Range Graph Benchmark (LRGB), consisting of five datasets specifically designed to evaluate Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) and Graph Transformers in their ability to capture long-range interactions on graph data. It identifies shortcomings in existing benchmarks, which often focus on local interactions, and emphasizes the importance of considering long-range dependencies for certain tasks. The datasets cover various domains, including computer vision and chemistry, and include tasks like node classification and link prediction.

sustainable_development_is_central.justification: The central theme of the paper is the development and benchmarking of Graph Neural Networks and Transformers to capture long-range interactions in graphs, rather than any direct focus or application to climate or ecological sustainable development.

new_primary_category.justification: The paper discusses the creation and use of datasets for evaluating AI models’ capabilities, specifically in terms of handling graph-based data with long-range dependencies.
new_primary_category.quote: We present the Long Range Graph Benchmark (LRGB) consisting of 5 datasets for node, edge and graph-level prediction tasks.

new_primary_sub_category.justification: The specific focus of the paper is on benchmarking Graph Neural Networks and Graph Transformers for their ability to model long-range interactions.
new_primary_sub_category.quote: Consequently, we introduce 5 benchmarking datasets – PascalVOC-SP, COCO-SP, PCQM-Contact, Peptides-func and Peptides-struct from the domains of Computer Vision and Chemistry.
